articles.title: If Manchester City are actually stripped of their three prized Premier League titles, which clubs will emerge as the new champions?
articles.summary: Explore the implications of Manchester City's financial charges verdict and potential title strip. Discover which teams could be recognized as champions if City loses their titles, including Manchester United and Liverpool.
articles.body: Manchester City’s reported guilty verdict on 114 of the 115 Premier League financial charges has reopened one of the biggest questions hanging over the case: if the club are eventually stripped of the titles they won during the period under investigation, who would actually be recognised as champions instead?The answer is not as straightforward as simply handing the trophies to the teams that finished second, particularly because no sanction has yet been decided, City are expected to appeal and the Premier League’s rules give an independent commission a wide range of options.Why City's three titles are now part of the discussionManchester City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 with 115 alleged breaches of its financial rules covering the period from 2009 to 2018. The independent commission’s hearing began on September 16, 2024, and ran for around three months before concluding in December 2024.On Friday, September 25, 2026, The Athletic reported that the commission had found City guilty on 114 of the 115 charges. Reuters subsequently reported the same finding, while noting that the club are expected to appeal and that the process is not yet complete. Manchester City have maintained that the Premier League process remains ongoing and that their position has not changed.No sanctions have been announced, meaning the reported verdict does not itself strip City of any trophy. The next stage will determine what punishment, if any, follows, with both sides having an appeal route under the Premier League rules.The reason the titles have become part of the conversation is the period covered by the charges. City won the Premier League three times between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, claiming their first title in 44 years in 2011/12 before winning again in 2013/14 and 2017/18.The first of those triumphs came in extraordinary fashion. City finished level on points with Manchester United in 2011/12 but won the title on goal difference, with Sergio Agüero's famous 94th-minute goal against Queens Park Rangers delivering the championship at the Etihad Stadium.Two years later, City finished two points ahead of Liverpool to win the 2013/14 title. Their third championship within the period came in 2017/18, when Pep Guardiola's side became the first Premier League team to reach 100 points.That leaves three seasons in which a retrospective title change could theoretically affect the final standings, should the commission ultimately impose a sanction that alters those results.Could Manchester City actually lose the titles?There is a legal route for retrospective sporting punishment, but that is different from saying title stripping is inevitable or even likely.Sub-clause W.51.7 of the Premier League handbook states that the commission can “impose upon the respondent any combination of the foregoing or such other penalty as it shall think fit”. According to The Athletic, the potential sanctions under Rule W.51 range from reprimands and financial penalties to points deductions and expulsion from the Premier League.The important detail is that points deductions can be imposed retrospectively, meaning the commission has a mechanism through which past league standings could potentially be affected. That is what creates the possibility, however remote, of City losing titles won during the period covered by the case.José Mourinho raised the possibility himself in October 2024, when his Manchester United side's 2017/18 campaign was brought up ahead of a Europa League meeting with Fenerbahçe.“As you know, we finished second in the Premier League [in 2018]," Mourinho said with a grin.“I think we still have a chance to win that league because maybe they punish Manchester City with points, and maybe we win that league and then they have to pay me the bonus and give me the medal.”The practical question is whether a retrospective points deduction would automatically result in another club being declared champion.Finance expert Kieran Maguire told Sky Sports in 2024 that it would be “difficult” for another club to establish that City's alleged breaches directly cost them silverware.“If you talk to lawyers, they will say it will be difficult for another club to say that they lost a title, or they lost probably more importantly access to the Champions League and the rewards that brings,” Maguire said.The issue was also discussed at the Business of Football Summit in 2025, where Sky reporter Rob Harris spoke with sports journalist Matt Hughes of FootBiz, sports lawyer Simon Leaf and The Sun reporter Martin Lipton.Hughes said: “There seems to be no appetite to take retrospective punishment.”Leaf was more cautious, saying it was still “too early” to reach a final view, while pointing to the potential financial claims from clubs that believe they missed out because of City's results.“I suspect there will be certain clubs looking at this and saying, actually we would have been entitled to payments for qualifying for Champions League... or even bonuses from sponsors from finishing in a different position,” Leaf said.Lipton, meanwhile, argued that removing the titles would go too far.“If you were to strip titles, the single most iconic moment in the history of the Premier League - Sergio Aguero's 94th minute goal against QPR to win the league - didn't happen,” he said.“You can't rewrite history to that extent.”Lipton added that title stripping was “not going to happen”.Which clubs finished second behind City?If the Premier League were to retrospectively alter the three title races in question, the runners-up provide the obvious starting point.2011/12 — Manchester UnitedManchester United finished level on points with City in 2011/12, with both clubs ending the season on 89 points. City took the title on goal difference after Agüero's extraordinary late winner against QPR.Sir Alex Ferguson's United therefore represent the most obvious alternative champion if the 2011/12 title were removed from City's record.It is also the title most deeply intertwined with the debate because of how it was decided. City did not simply finish ahead of United by a comfortable margin; they were separated by goal difference after one of the most famous finishes in Premier League history.2013/14 — LiverpoolLiverpool finished second in 2013/14, two points behind City.Brendan Rodgers' side had led the title race for much of the season and appeared on course to win their first Premier League championship before a late-season collapse allowed City to overtake them.A retrospective alteration would therefore put Liverpool in the position of the team immediately behind City in the final table, although, as Maguire and the other experts have pointed out, being the original runner-up does not necessarily mean a club is automatically entitled to receive the title years later.2017/18 — Manchester UnitedManchester United finished second again in 2017/18, this time 19 points behind Guardiola's record-breaking City side.Mourinho's comments in 2024 specifically referred to this season and his belief that United could still theoretically be awarded the title if City were punished retrospectively.So, if the runners-up were simply retrospectively promoted into the vacant championship places, the hypothetical list would be:2011/12: Manchester United2013/14: Liverpool2017/18: Manchester UnitedThat is a possible scenario rather than a confirmed outcome. There is currently no announced decision stating that these three clubs will inherit City's titles if sanctions are imposed.What punishment could Manchester City face?The reported finding of 114 guilty charges has moved the case into its next stage, but it has not established what punishment City will receive. The independent commission has a range of sanctions available under the Premier League's rules, and the club are expected to appeal the verdict.The potential punishments listed in the Premier League handbook are:Suspend a club from playing league matchesPoints deductionsRecommend to the board that league matches be replayedRecommend to the board that the league expels the respondent clubOrder compensationCancel or refuse registration of playersConditional punishmentOrder the club to pay costsMake such other order as it thinks fitFor now, the three title races remain officially unchanged: Manchester City are the champions of 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2017/18. The possibility of Manchester United receiving two of those titles and Liverpool receiving the other exists only if the eventual disciplinary process produces that outcome.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘They cannot take out of us’: Rodri breaks silence as former club Man City face losing three Premier League titles
articles.summary: Rodri, the former midfielder for Manchester City, speaks out in support of the club following its guilty verdict on 114 financial breaches, insisting their achievements cannot be erased as the legal process continues.
articles.body: Rodri has become the first prominent former Manchester City player to publicly address the club's 114-charge verdict, and the former midfielder is standing firmly behind his old side. City were found guilty of 114 of the 115 Premier League financial rule breaches brought against them, but Rodri says he continues to believe the club are innocent and will wait for the legal process to run its course.Rodri stands by City's innocenceSpeaking at a press conference ahead of Spain's Nations League match against England, Rodri was asked about the verdict after the independent commission found City guilty of the majority of the charges relating to the period between 2009 and 2018.The former City midfielder, who made 298 appearances for the club between 2019 and 2026, said the club had consistently maintained its innocence and that he had no reason to change his position.“They always express the confidence that they never did something wrong, and we believe in that,” Rodri said.“Until the moment they are proved wrong, we will believe the club. They always tell us the confidence they have on the innocence.”Rodri then pointed to City's previous experience with UEFA's financial regulations as a reason for maintaining that position.City were initially given a two-year ban from European competitions by UEFA in February 2020 after being found to have committed “serious breaches” of UEFA's club licensing and financial fair play regulations. The Court of Arbitration for Sport later overturned the ban after City appealed, although the club were still fined €10 million for failing to cooperate with UEFA's investigation.Rodri said the episode influenced the way he views the current Premier League case.“We had the example of 2020 that the process was the same, and at the end nothing happened,” he explained.“We have faced something similar; we had a similar judicial process – different accusation, but similar process.“There as well, in the first instance, we were found guilty, but we believed in the club and the innocence that the club maintained, and in the end we ended up acquitted.“So, I believe in the justice system, and I believe in the innocence of the club.”City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023, with the allegations covering nine seasons between 2009 and 2018. During that period, the club won three Premier League titles, three League Cups, one Community Shield and one FA Cup.Rodri says City's achievements cannot be taken awayThe possibility of Manchester City being stripped of those Premier League titles has become one of the most contentious questions following the verdict, although no sanctions have yet been decided and City are expected to appeal.Rodri was asked directly about the possibility of the club losing its silverware and made clear that he does not believe the achievements of the players involved can simply be erased.“What we did, they cannot take out of us,” Rodri said.“It’s something that is not paid by money. It’s paid with effort, with the damage, with, you know, being shoulder to shoulder every day.”“I can tell you that everything was deserved, and I’m glad that I could live one of the best eras of English football in here.”Rodri was part of City's Premier League-winning team in 2020/21, 2021/22 and 2022/23, meaning his own honours at the club came largely after the period covered by the charges. He joined City in 2019 and left for Barcelona in 2026 after six seasons in Manchester.Manchester City maintain their positionManchester City responded to the verdict on Friday by reiterating that the Premier League process remains ongoing and that the club's position has not changed since the charges were brought in 2023.“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023,” the club said.“The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”City have consistently denied wrongdoing since the Premier League brought the charges against them, maintaining that they possess a “body of irrefutable evidence” supporting their defence.The independent commission has yet to determine the sanctions arising from the 114 findings, while City are expected to appeal the verdict. Until that process is completed, the club's titles remain officially intact and Rodri's position is unchanged: he continues to believe Manchester City are innocent.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England 2-3 Spain: Thomas Tuchel rues 'big mistakes' - did Man City charges have impact?
articles.summary: England's loss to Spain was decided by uncharacteristic mistakes, with two Man City players making errors - so did club news affect performances for country?
articles.body:
It was a match full of world-class players - but England's loss to Spain was ultimately decided by uncharacteristic mistakes.

Just a day after Manchester City were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules, two errors by City players - Nico O'Reilly and Marc Guehi - gifted world champions Spain two goals.

And former City midfielder Rodri, who moved to Barcelona in the summer, also gave away a penalty in Spain's 3-2 win on Saturday.

Pundit Roy Keane was among those left to wonder whether news of the verdict had affected players with City ties.

Asked if it was a distraction after his side's loss at Wembley, England boss Thomas Tuchel said: "Not for me but I can imagine for the Manchester City players.

"For the players who have more time than me, for sure I can imagine they talk about it."

Speaking to ITV Sport former Manchester United captain Keane said: "In top level football you want to be focused and they certainly would have been affected.

"To see so many top-class players make so many mistakes - it has certainly affected them."

Man City and the 115 charges - key questions answered

Man City chairman confident club will prove innocence

Man City fans face up to reality of guilty verdict

Three City players - Elliot Anderson, Guehi and O'Reilly - started for England, while Rodri, who spent seven years at the club, was in Spain's XI.

And three of those four players made significant errors at Wembley.

First Guehi was tackled by Lamine Yamal on the edge of his own box, allowing the Spain winger to drive towards goal and slot in his side's opener.

In the second half Rodri's late challenge on Jude Bellingham led to an England penalty, which Harry Kane struck against the crossbar after slipping.

And then O'Reilly had a pass intercepted deep in his own half which led to Alex Baena's equaliser at 2-2.

On Friday, sources told BBC Sport City had been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching.

After a four-year investigation, the club were accused of a wide range of rule breaches centring around claims they inflated sponsorship revenue and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

Sanctions are yet to be announced, but repercussions could include a points deduction, expulsion from the Premier League or a huge fine.

BBC Sport understands Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice about potential compensation.

England captain Kane played down any links between the charges and player mistakes, telling ITV Sport after Saturday's game: "There was a discussion, but at the end of the day when we're with England we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week."

A few hours before kick-off at Wembley, City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak told supporters he was still confident of proving the club's innocence and the "Premier League process still has a long way to run".

Spain captain Rodri had also stressed his belief in the club's innocence in a news conference on Friday.

"They always express the confidence that they never did something wrong and we believe in that," he said.

"Until the moment they are proved wrong, we will believe the club. They always tell us the confidence they have on the innocence."

The charges cover the managerial tenures of Roberto Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini, and the first two years under Pep Guardiola, who left the club after 10 seasons at the end of the 2025-26 campaign.

City won the Premier League and EFL Cup three times and FA Cup once between 2009 and 2018.

Guehi, Rodri and O'Reilly all made their City debuts after the period in question.

articles.title: Texas Trolls Johnny Knoxville With 'Jackass' Video After Tennessee Pick on 'College GameDay'
articles.summary: Stunt performer and actor Johnny Knoxville was College GameDay's celebrity guest picker on Saturday.
articles.body:
Stunt performer and actor Johnny Knoxville was College GameDay's celebrity guest picker on Saturday.

There's no surprise that Knoxville, who was born and raised in the Tennessee city and adopted his professional name after it, picked his host Volunteers to beat No. 1 Texas.

Tennessee put up a good fight but ultimately lost 20-17. After the game, Texas trolled Knoxville with a video in the theme of his famous Jackass franchise.

Knoxville got the pick wrong, but he was certainly entertaining, even dressing up as a Volunteer.

ESPN also harkened back to the infamous Jackass moment when he fielded punts and got clobbered against the USC Trojans 25 years ago.

Knoxville's Volunteers will look to bounce back next Saturday at home against Auburn.

articles.title: Oklahoma QB John Mateer coughs up ball 3 times in second quarter; No. 2 Georgia romps struggling Sooners
articles.summary: Mateer's interception was sandwiched by a pair of fumbles, one of which Bulldogs LB Chris Cole returned 85 yards to the house.
articles.body:
The second quarter of Saturday's game between No. 2 Georgia and Oklahoma couldn't have gone much worse for Sooners quarterback John Mateer .

He turned the ball over three times, throwing one pick and losing a pair of fumbles.

The first of those giveaways was the most embarrassing.

With Oklahoma trailing 14-0 and threatening to make it a one-score game, the fifth-year signal-caller coughed the ball up near the goal line. He rolled to the left off a play fake, opened his hips as if he was going to throw, then proceeded briefly before trying to attempt a pass that never was.

The ball slipped out of his hand, bounced backward and was collected by Georgia linebacker Chris Cole , who galloped for an 85-yard scoop-and-score.

That 14-point swing made it 21-0 in the Bulldogs ' favor. Georgia (4-0, 2-0 SEC) ran away with a 41-13 victory at home.

Oklahoma (2-2, 0-1) went 2 of 14 on third down, 1 of 3 on fourth down and committed 4 turnovers, off which the Bulldogs scored 17 points.

Cole had himself a banner day. Midway through the third quarter, he already had six solo tackles and a sack. He finished with eight total tackles, including seven solos. Plus, the 6-foot-3, 235-pound junior flew like the wind en route to that defensive score.

He also picked up Mateer's next fumble, later in the quarter.

Facing a fourth-and-1 from the Oklahoma 43-yard line, Mateer faked an end around and evaded a blitzing Cole, only to then be wrapped up by linebacker Raylen Wilson , who jarred the rock loose by the sideline.

It stayed inbounds, as Cole gathered the fumble and raced 23 yards to the Sooners' 11, giving him 108 total yards on fumble returns Saturday.

Two plays after that, running back Chauncey Bowens found the end zone on a 6-yard rush to extend Georgia's lead to 28-0.

Sandwiched in between those fumbles was Mateer's pick. On third-and-9 from the Bulldogs' 43, Oklahoma snapped the ball to Mateer in shotgun. Soon enough, his clean pocket collapsed.

By the time he fired, he had a defender in his face. His pass over the middle was well short of wide receiver Jacob Jordan and was nabbed by Bulldogs safety KJ Bolden , who broke a couple tackles on a 29-yard interception return .

Mateer, a former Washington State QB who was a Heisman Trophy favorite early in his first go-around with the Sooners, is off to a head-scratching start in 2026. He came into the campaign healthy after navigating a hand injury that required surgery and clearly affected him down the stretch last season.

And yet, he completed merely 51.5% of his passes in a 17-10 loss to a Michigan team that was unranked following its near loss to Western Michigan in Week 1.

Last week, against Mountain West upstart New Mexico , Mateer tossed a pair of interceptions. The Sooners barely won that game, 14-10.

Since a 51-0 shutout in its season opener versus UTEP, Oklahoma has scored a combined 37 points in its past three games.

Meanwhile, Georgia is coasting through the first part of its regular-season slate. It wasn't perfect Saturday, either, but its defense and 130 rushing yards were enough to make a sizable difference.

articles.title: No. 17 Iowa stuns No. 18 Michigan with last-second touchdown to earn 20-19 win and stay undefeated
articles.summary: The Hawkeyes scored a touchdown with 2 seconds remaining, earning the 1-point win and breaking hearts in Ann Arbor.
articles.body:
Sometimes, what goes around comes around. In a high-profile matchup between No. 17 Iowa and No. 18 Michigan , a slow start made way for a wild ending as the Hawkeyes pulled off a miraculous last-second touchdown.

Michigan, which pulled out to a five-point lead in the fourth quarter, tried to hold off a late Iowa push. But as time expired, Hawkeyes quarterback Hank Brown found Reece Vander Zee in the end zone, with the receiver perfectly staying in bounds to give Iowa a 20-19 win.

Earlier in the drive, the Wolverines ' defense had appeared to put a nail in the coffin by forcing third-and-long with less than 30 seconds left. But a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty — thanks to a late shove out of bounds from Michigan cornerback Zeke Berry — gave Iowa another chance. Brown kept the drive alive with a pass to Addison Ostrenga, who tipped the ball to himself for a 29-yard catch and left just enough time on the clock to dash the Wolverines' dreams.

It was an ending slightly reminiscent — though the Wolverines were on the other side — of Michigan's season-opening win over Western Michigan , when the officials' controversial addition of a single second gave the Wolverines the chance for a game-winning Hail Mary . The NCAA later admitted that mistakes had been made in the officiating process.

After the win, Iowa's social media account appeared to note some of the similarities as well.

Saturday's matchup between the two Big Ten defensive heavyweights promised to be a low-scoring game. That turned out to be about halfway true: The offense-adverse Iowa racked up just 285 yards compared to Michigan's 429 total offensive yards. But the Hawkeyes' defense showed up in several key moments to limit the Wolverines, and make way for the game-winning play.

For much of the fourth quarter, it didn't look like Iowa would be able to pull it off. After quarterback Bryce Underwood 's 49-yard go-ahead touchdown pass to JJ Buchanan , the Hawkeyes initially stuck to the Kirk Ferentz brand of avoiding risks: With 2 ½ minutes left in the game, Iowa opted to kick a 51-yard field goal on fourth-and-6 despite being down five points. Caden Buhr's attempt then went wide.

Thanks to the Michigan home crowd, the Hawkeyes also had three key false start penalties in the second half, including one that put Iowa at third-and-long late before Berry's unnecessary roughness penalty bailed them out.

Postgame, Ferentz was visibly emotional as he praised his players for not giving up.

"One thing about these guys, they don't quit. They fight. It wasn't perfect, but they don't give up," Ferentz said.

Michigan's offense, which has been an obvious weak point for the team early on, looked much more solid even in the loss: Underwood went 17-for-28 passing with 276 yards and 2 touchdowns as his connections with Buchanan and receiver Andrew Marsh continued to sparkle.

But in the end, the Hawkeyes (and, perhaps, Western Michigan) got the last laugh.

articles.title: Grading Jared Curtis after Vanderbilt football loss to Auburn
articles.summary: Here's how we graded freshman quarterback Jared Curtis after Vanderbilt football 's 21-15 loss to Auburn.
articles.body:
AUBURN, AL ― Jared Curtis made his first SEC start for Vanderbilt football in a 21-15 loss to Auburn at Jordan-Hare Stadium on Sept. 26.

It was the Commodores ' first loss of the season (3-1, 0-1).

Curtis put up a relatively mistake-free performance despite the offense overall being plagued by penalties and struggling to run the ball.

Here's how we graded Curtis' performance:

Jared Curtis, Vanderbilt football QB, one of nation's top 2026 recruits

Curtis was 22-for-33 for 199 yards, no touchdowns and one interception, which came on an attempted Hail Mary at the end of the first half.

He ran 14 times for 69 yards, not including sacks.

He was sacked four times for a total of 23 yards.

Vanderbilt had several offensive issues against Auburn (3-1, 1-1), but those were more about penalties and an inability to get a traditional run game going than it was about Curtis.

He was the Commodores ' most effective rusher of the day, as he was frequently able to find open space via scrambles and he evaded tacklers. He avoided errors, but also didn't have as many explosive downfield throws as he did against NC State, more frequently missing open shots and completing only two passes of more than 15 yards. His efficiency came despite frequently facing heavy pressure.

Curtis might not have been the problem with Vanderbilt's offense, but he also was unable to take over the game once the Commodores got behind.

articles.title: Michigan football winners, losers as special teams flub too costly
articles.summary: Free Press sports writer Rainer Sabin highlights the best and worst performances from No. 18 Michigan football's 20-19 loss to No. 17 Iowa.
articles.body:
Free Press sports writer Rainer Sabin highlights the best and worst performances from No. 18 Michigan football 's 20-19 loss to No. 17 Iowa on Saturday, Sept. 26, at Michigan Stadium.

Ever since his rough 2026 debut against Western Michigan, Underwood has looked more competent and poised while operating the Wolverines ' offense. On Saturday, he jumped out to a fast start, connecting on eight of his first 10 throws for 118 yards and a touchdown. If not for a Salesi Moa drop on Underwood's second pass attempt, Underwood's completion percentage would have even been higher. Coordinator Jason Beck put Underwood in position to succeed by utilizing his athleticism. On several occasions, he called plays with designed rollouts that gave Underwood clear throwing lanes downfield. Beck also creatively deployed Underwood in a Wildcat package, lining him up out wide and having him flash across the formation in a jet motion. In one instance, Underwood took a handoff from running back Jordan Marshall and then completed an 11-yard pass to Andrew Marsh . Later in the half, Beck dipped again into his bag of tricks, dialing up a flea-flicker. Underwood executed it to perfection, feathering a layered pass to JJ Buchanan for a 32-yard gain.

In the fourth quarter, after Iowa took the one-point lead, Underwood maneuvered in the pocket, evaded a few oncoming rushers and delivered a 49-yard strike to Buchanan to put the Wolverines ahead, 19-14.

It seemed at that point his touchdown pass would carry Michigan to its fourth win. Alas, it was not meant to be . Still, Underwood could walk away knowing he authored one of the best performances of his career. He finished the game with 17 completions on 28 attempts, 276 passing yards, two touchdowns and an interception.

While no one would claim Michigan has an elite passing offense, the Wolverines do have a pair of talented wideouts who possess dynamic playmaking ability.

That was evident Saturday, as Marsh and Buchanan took turns singing Iowa 's defense.

On Michigan's second possession, Marsh helped carry Michigan into Hawkeyes territory with two catches that totaled 47 yards. The second one was a remarkable feat of athleticism, as Marsh leapt to snag a pass from Underwood along the sideline while managing to keep one of his feet inbounds. In a game like this one, where the margin for error was expected to be thin, Michigan couldn't afford many mistakes.

But the Wolverines had a major breakdown a few seconds after they took a 7-0 lead in the first quarter. On the kickoff that followed Buchanan's 18-yard touchdown catch, Iowa returner Braeden Jackson fielded the ball at the 1, veered right and found an alley. By the time he reached the 30, he was in the clear. Jackson zipped all the way to the end zone. The 99-yard return tied the score and stunned the home crowd.

It also reverberated for the rest of the game, keeping Iowa within striking distance of the Wolverines and boosting a team that managed to produce just 129 yards through the first three quarters.

Throughout its history, Michigan has extracted a lot of production out of its tight ends. Two years ago, Colston Loveland led the Wolverines in receiving en route to an NFL draft first-round selection.

But through the first three games, U-M's passing game was powered almost entirely by U-M's wide receivers and running backs.

Jalen Hoffman was the lone tight end to catch a pass and he accounted for just two receptions for 22 yards. On Tuesday, when asked what needed to change for his position group to become more involved, sophomore Eli Owens said, "Obviously, what jumps off the page is we need to get open. I mean, that's everybody in the room. We need to get open. That's simply what it is."

Michigan tight ends again weren't much of a factor Saturday against Iowa.

Collectively, they contributed just four catches for 21 yards.

For much of the game, the Wolverines' fifth-year player was one of Michigan's top performers.

Targeted seven times, he allowed just three catches for 15 yards. He also produced two pass breakups, according to Pro Football Focus.

But none of that mattered when he committed an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty during Iowa's final drive, shoving receiver Tony Diaz after a pass toward the sideline fell incomplete. If the foul had not been committed, Iowa would have faced fourth-and-12 at its own 40. Instead the Hawkeyes began a new set of downs at Michigan's 45. Four snaps after that pivotal moment, Iowa quarterback Hank Brown connected with Reece Vander Zee for on a 16-yard touchdown pass as time expired, lifting the Hawkeyes to an improbable one-point victory.

Certainly, Berry was not the sole reason why the Wolverines lost. But his penalty helped position the Hawkeyes to steal the win.

articles.title: Pete Golding questions Ole Miss defense's manhood after Florida runs over Rebels
articles.summary: Pete Golding questioned the Ole Miss defense's manhood and courage after giving up over 300 rushing yards in blowout loss to Florida and Jadan Baugh
articles.body:
GAINESVILLE, FL — Ole Miss football coach Pete Golding was displeased with his team's tackling method in the Rebels' 52-28 loss to Florida .

"The thing at halftime that I addressed was we had a lot of guys trying to ankle bite, and diving at ankles and all those things," Golding said. "I addressed the manhood at halftime a little bit. There was a lack of courage, in my opinion, at times that we were picking and choosing."

Ole Miss football vs Florida, Trinidad Chambliss, Jadan Baugh see our best photos

No. 22 Florida beat No. 6 Ole Miss on Sept. 26 at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. The Gators racked up 302 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns. Star running back Jadan Baugh had 142 yards and three touchdowns.

"That's an elite back and he's a big back," Golding said. "You've got to go chest-to-chest with him."

The Gators scored the most points on the Rebels in six years, dating back to Dec. 19, 2020, in a 53-58 loss at LSU .

"We just didn't get our players to execute," Golding said. "That goes back to coaching. I told our players we've got to look in the mirror as well, so we're all accountable to it and go back and clean this thing up."

articles.title: Why Vanderbilt football used Blaze Berlowitz at wide receiver vs Auburn
articles.summary: Here's why Vanderbilt football used backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz at wide receiver in a loss to Auburn.
articles.body:
AUBURN, AL ― Vanderbilt football used Blaze Berlowitz at wide receiver during its game against Auburn , a trend that could continue throughout the season.

Berlowitz, who started the season at quarterback for the Commodores (3-1, 0-1 SEC) saw two targets at receiver. He caught one pass but did not gain any yards, and the second throw was incomplete.

Coach Clark Lea said after Vanderbilt's 21-15 loss to Auburn (3-1, 1-1) on Sept. 26 at Jordan-Hare Stadium that Berlowitz approached the coaching staff about getting reps at receiver as an additional way to help the team. Berlowitz is also prepared to step in for Jared Curtis at quarterback if needed.

"Blaze is such an important part of our team," Lea said. " . . . When you look at his strength measures and speed measures and power measures, this guy is one of the most explosive athletes we have on our team, and so it makes all the sense in the world that we're going to find a way to use him, and also that he's going to be prepared to play quarterback, too, he knows the system, and so I'm not concerned about reps that he's taken out on the perimeter . . . I think he's going to have a chance to help us win."

Berlowitz was 14-for-25 passing for 178 yards passing in two games. He ran 13 times for 50 yards with one rushing touchdown. He started games against Austin Peay and Delaware before Curtis won the starting job. Since Curtis was named the starter, Berlowitz has not played.

"This is a guy that comes in and says, 'I want to help this team win, I know I can do it,' and I have the utmost respect for that guy," Lea said. "He is such a good person, such a great competitor, and he wants to help this team win . . . I'm looking forward to him expanding that role as we move through the season."

Aria Gerson covers Vanderbilt athletics for The Tennessean. Contact her at agerson@gannett.com or on X @aria_gerson .

articles.title: Iowa football news: Hawkeyes shock Michigan with epic last-second touchdown
articles.summary: Iowa football improved its College Football Playoff chances and shocked the Michigan Wolverines with a 20-19 Week 4 road win that came in the most thrilling...
articles.body:
Iowa football improved its College Football Playoff chances and shocked the Michigan Wolverines with a 20-19 Week 4 road win that came in the most thrilling of ways. The Hawkeyes got a last-second touchdown pass from recently appointed starting QB Hank Brown to receiver Reece Vander Zee that sent 111,000 plus fans home with memories they will likely never forget.

Reporter Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports shared video of the exciting play , which gave the Hawkeyes their first win in the series since 2016.

Brown battled Jeremy Hecklinksi throughout training camp before coming out on top and gaining the opportunity to show Hawkeyes fans what he can do this season. The former three-star quarterback from Nashville, Tennessee has now led coach Kirk Ferentz 's team to four consecutive wins.

Brown had his best game against the Wolverines, completing 21-of-35 passes for 227 yards and two touchdowns on a day when his Wolverines counterpart Bryce Underwood had 276 yards passing, two touchdowns and an interception.

Michigan outgained Iowa by a final tally of 429 to 285 total yards, but the Wolverines failed to capitalize on their opportunities and allowed Ferentz's team to hang around. A Braeden Jackson 99-yard first quarter kickoff return also helped seal the Wolverines' losing fate as the Hawkeyes ruled the day in Ann Arbor, sending coach Kyle Whittingham's team back to the drawing board.

Brown, Vander Zee and Ferentz's team now have coach Ryan Day and the Ohio State Buckeyes ' full and undivided attention as Ohio State will take on the No. 17 Hawkeyes on October 3 in Iowa City. A win in that game could make Iowa one of the nation's top ranked teams, an unthinkable early season scenario for a program that didn't know who its quarterback would be just a few short months ago.

For a quarter and a half, it looked like it was going to be another listless Wisconsin loss under Luke Fickell. Then it became the biggest win of the coach's tenure in Madison.

The unranked Badgers overcame a 17-0 deficit to upset No. 13 Penn State on the road, capping things off with a 72 yard pass from Colton Joseph to Jacob Harris with less than two minutes left. It left Penn State with enough time for a last-minute drive, but that ended with a Hail Mary bouncing incomplete as time expired.

Final score: Wisconsin 24, Penn State 20.

articles.title: UND holds off Indiana State comeback to win 42-35
articles.summary: Sep. 26—TERRE HAUTE, Ind. — The UND football team's sixth of six flights through three time zones in the last three weeks might not be a full-on midair celeb...
articles.body:
Sep. 26—TERRE HAUTE, Ind. — The UND football team's sixth of six flights through three time zones in the last three weeks might not be a full-on midair celebration Saturday evening, but the Fighting Hawks will still get out of Wabash Valley with a win — and that's not always been a given at Memorial Stadium.

The No. 7 Fighting Hawks nearly coughed up a three-touchdown lead in the fourth quarter before surviving a late push from Indiana State with a 42-35 victory in front of 2,765.

UND players and coaches wrestled postgame with the dynamic: UND will return home from the road trip with a Missouri Valley Football Conference win and a 4-1 record, but there was also plenty of concerning mistakes, too.

"We're going through an interesting time right now," UND coach Eric Schmidt said. "You got a chance here in a couple of games now to really put some people away. Up 42-21 in the fourth quarter, and you think you're putting some things together, then you just do some things football-wise that we've got — I've got — to do a better job. Our team's got to do a better job.

"Defensively, you can't let up explosive plays. The onside kick. Kicking the ball out of bounds. It's been a long three weeks here, and it's just a grind. We have to do a better job playing consistently and playing confidently."

UND quarterback Jerry Kaminski threw for a career-high 381 yards on 33-for-48 passing with four touchdowns. He hit Cameron Weir for a 39-yard deep ball to give the Hawks a 42-21 lead with 9 minutes, 37 seconds left in the game.

"The biggest thing for us is it's hard to win a college football game, especially on the road and then you talk about a Missouri Valley Football Conference away game," Kaminski said. "We battled. I'm proud of the guys for the way we fought, but we know we have a lot of things that we can clean up, and we're excited to attack the process and get back to it tomorrow."

The Sycamores scored 96 seconds after UND's three-touchdown lead when Jayden Reed caught a 33-yard touchdown pass from Brady Allen to cut the lead to 42-28.

Indiana State then recovered an onside kick as UND's hands team didn't attack the bounding ball, allowing the Sycamores to recover. From there, Allen struck again. This time, the new starting quarterback, playing in place of injured starter Elijah Owens, connected with B.J. Wuest for a 17-yard touchdown connection.

Wuest's score trimmed the UND lead to 42-35 with 6:36 left in the game.

The Hawks' offense couldn't ice the win on its next drive. After picking up one first down, the Hawks punted the ball back to Indiana State with more than three minutes to go — needing 89 yards to tie or win the game.

After picking up one first down, UND's defense forced incompletions on third-and-4 and fourth-and-4 to finally turn the Sycamores over on downs. UND was able to ice the rest of the clock after taking over at the ISU 34 with 1:52 left in the game.

"There's just a lot to learn from," said UND edge Braden Mohr, who had three sacks. "A win is a win. It's a tough place to win. They're all tough in the Valley. We're excited but we know when we get back we have a lot to learn, too. We just have to make sure we're playing our game, and we don't let other teams influence us. I think when we're playing our game, we're going to be successful, but when we allow teams to dictate the game, that's when we struggle a little bit."

The Hawks held the Sycamores to 44 rushing yards on 28 attempts. Yet, Allen, an FBS transfer making his first start, threw for 270 yards and four touchdowns. Reed finished with eight catches for 129 yards and two touchdowns.

"We lack a little continuity together," Schmidt said of his defensive evaluation. "When I watch us pressure and things like that, it's taking too long to get there and be able to beat some one-on-ones. We've got to look at some things there with what we're doing. I think too the discipline of being able to do simple things ... like I'm watching some of our underneath coverage, and it's guys just kind of wandering around and not dropping the proper depths. Even when we're in decent position, we're grabbing and holding. Those are the things that we've got to continue to get better at. We're not a finished product yet. I think we have the opportunity to be better there yet. We need to be better."

articles.title: Mistakes, injuries sink Michigan State in frustrating loss to Nebraska
articles.summary: Michigan State football made too many mistakes and suffered too many injuries in a Week 4 loss to Nebraska at Spartan Stadium on Saturday, Sept. 26.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING – Michigan State football made too many mistakes and suffered too many injuries to have a chance in a 31-13 Week 4 loss to Nebraska at Spartan Stadium on Saturday, Sept. 26.

The Spartans lost their best player on offense ( Cam Edwards , knee), their best player on defense ( Jordan Hall , leg) and were playing without the top-four cornerbacks in the frustrating game vs. the Cornhuskers . They also had two fumbles (one lost) and two interceptions, not to mention multiple costly penalties.

At times, the Spartans looked like they belonged, but there were some bad mistakes and some bad breaks that ultimately were too much to overcome in what ended up being an ugly game.

MSU's defense, which has been decimated by injuries at cornerback and already playing without starting linebacker Brady Pretzlaff before the injury to Hall, held in the fight, producing stops on the first three drives to start the second half.

After scoring a field goal on their first drive after the break, the Spartans fumbled on their second drive and then were driving down the field on their third drive when tight end Jayden Savoury made what looked like an incredible catch to get the Spartans into prime scoring position, but the catch was ultimately overturned by a tough review.

Quarterback Alessio Milivojevic , who was under pressure all day with six Nebraska sacks, fumbled again and though it was recovered by MSU this time, the Spartans missed their 52-yard field goal attempt to come out empty handed, and the Cornhuskers cruised to a victory from there.

The Spartans return to the road to face Wisconsin next Saturday, Oct. 3 in Madison, Wisconsin (12:30 p.m./BTN). This will be the first time MSU has faced a Luke Fickell coached team since he spurned the Spartans for a chance to replace Mark Dantonio after he retired in February 2020. Fickell instead remained at Cincinnati until he took over in Madison in 2023.

The Badgers (2-1, who lost their opener to Notre Dame), opened conference play at No. 14 Penn State on Saturday concurrent with the MSU-Nebraska game. Fickell, in his fourth season at Wisconsin, entered Saturday with a 19-22 overall record and a 10-17 Big Ten record. Dantonio and MSU beat Ohio State , 10-7, in 2011 when Fickell was interim head coach after Jim Tressel's firing.

articles.title: Dante Moore Injured on Illegal Hit, Latest Updates After Oregon QB Was Transported to Hospital
articles.summary: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore was stretchered off the field, loaded into an ambulance and transported to the hospital after suffering an injury on a violent hit during the No. 20 Ducks' matchup with No. 12 USC on Saturday.
articles.body:
Oregon quarterback Dante Moore was stretchered off the field, loaded into an ambulance and transported to the hospital after suffering an injury on a violent hit during the No. 20 Ducks' matchup with No. 12 USC on Saturday.

Moore was hit above the shoulders by Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens II as he was sliding after scrambling for a first down in the second quarter.

Moore was transported to Los Angeles General County Hospital for further evaluation. According to the NBC broadcast , Moore has feeling in all of his extremities.

"He's moving, he has the ability to move, so we'll continue to assess him, but I don't want to make any speculation on further thoughts on that until we have more information with him," Oregon head coach Dan Lanning said after the Ducks' 41-27 win.

Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore under center.

After Raiola helped finish Oregon's drive with a touchdown, he threw up Moore's No. 5 with his right hand to support his teammate.

Moore was 8-of-10 for 77 yards before exiting the contest.

The 21-year-old's absence is a tough blow to Oregon's offense. He started his 2026 campaign on a high note after choosing to forgo the NFL draft and return to the Ducks on Jan. 14.

In Moore's first three games this season, he completed 68.5 percent of his passes for 849 yards and nine touchdowns without getting picked off. Oregon posted a 2-1 record over that span.

Moore was projected to be off the board with the No. 4 overall pick in the latest 2027 mock draft from Bleacher Report's NFL Scouting Department.

While he's sidelined, Raiola will help lead the Ducks' offense.

Raiola is in the midst of his first season at Oregon but has plenty of experience, previously serving as Nebraska's starting quarterback from 2024-25.

In 22 games with the Cornhuskers, he completed 69.1 percent of his throws for 4,819 yards and 31 touchdowns compared to 17 interceptions.

articles.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore leaves game vs. USC with apparent head injury after violent hit
articles.summary: The back of Moore's head hit the ground after he was hit while sliding.
articles.body:
Oregon's Dante Moore was injured in the second quarter of the No. 20 Ducks' game against No. 12 USC after he took a hit to the head while sliding on a scramble.

Moore's head violently hit the ground after he went into the slide on a hit by Desman Stephens II that drew an immediate flag. The teams had to be separated after the hit as Oregon players were furious and other flags were thrown.

After training staff attended to Moore on the field for several minutes, he was taken to a waiting cart on a backboard. Moore was greeted by numerous teammates after he was loaded onto the cart and, per the NBC broadcast, was moving his arms.

An ambulance was driven out of the tunnel at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum and Moore was placed into it.

Stephens was ejected for targeting. The entirety of both Oregon and USC's teams were assessed personal fouls for the post-hit kerfuffle.

Moore was replaced by Dylan Raiola . The former Nebraska QB transferred to Oregon in the offseason. Two plays after he entered, Raiola threw a play-action TD pass to Evan Stewart to give the Ducks a 10-7 lead.

Moore entered the season as one of the favorites for the 2026 Heisman Trophy after he decided to return to school. He had a chance to be a top-two pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but chose to remain with Oregon after the Ducks were eliminated in the semifinals of the College Football Playoff by eventual national champion Indiana.

In his first season as a starter in 2025, Moore completed 72% of his passes for 3,565 yards and 30 TDs with 10 interceptions. Entering Week 4, Moore had thrown for 849 yards and nine touchdowns with no interceptions.

articles.title: The Florida Gators Are the National Championship Threat We Never Saw Coming
articles.summary: The easy thing to do would declare Florida "back," just like we did with Texas and Miami over the course of the last few seasons as these proud programs found life and simply move on.
articles.body:
The easy thing to do would declare Florida "back," just like we did with Texas and Miami over the course of the last few seasons as these proud programs found life and simply move on.

In truth, however, being "back" doesn't fully encapsulate what Florida did on Saturday. It also fails to fully capture what we're seeing and what it all means moving forward.

No, after what we just witnessed, the complete and thorough demolition of the hottest team in college football, the Gators deserve something more.

First, the final score. The Gators dropped a 50-burger and 498 yards on Ole Miss, beating the Rebels 52-28.

It's been years since Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, one of the sport's best, loudest venues, felt a renewed sense of life that has been long dormant.

The performance largely featured what we've seen all year. In some ways, we shouldn't be all that surprised.

Running back Jadan Baugh was once again dominant, running for 142 yards and three touchdowns. The Florida wide receivers, one of the deepest and most athletic in the sport, did what they've done for the past month.

And Aaron Philo, the Gators unappreciated quarterback, did everything he was supposed to do and then some. While other quarterbacks in the SEC have largely dominated early headlines, Philo's early brilliance won't be understated much longer.

The defense was good enough against Trinidad Chambliss, which is saying plenty. While this version of Florida is likely never to be defined on that side of the ball, it certainly did its part to make one of the game's most explosive players uncomfortable.

The architect of it all, Jon Sumrall, has been animated since he arrived. And following the victory, when pressed on what this could mean, he didn't shy away.

"We came here to win championships," Sumrall said following the game. "But there's no reason in the world that shouldn't be the expectation at the University of Florida every year. So why wait? I'm not real patient, you can ask my wife."

This was not the conversations we expected to have early on or ever with this team, and the expectations for Florida heading into the season weren't exactly sparkling. Given the way this blueblood has played in recent years, it's not hard to see why.

The days of Urban Meyer and Tim Tebow were long lost. Florida hasn't won more than eight games since 2019, and it's finished under .500 in four of those years.

This team hasn't just been average; it's been downright bad.

At the very least, one thing is clear after one month of football. The Gators are a factor in the SEC and one of the most dangerous teams in the country.

On a day that Georgia dominated Oklahoma and Texas toppled Tennessee on the road, it was Gainesville that delivered the biggest spectacle of all.

Sure, the Bulldogs look like a problem once again. Kirby Smart appears to have another talented roster to work with, and that theme will carry forward. But Georgia has yet to have the kind of challenge that the Gators just easily walked through.

As for Texas, there's plenty to like. The Longhorns' defense looks legitimate, and the offense, led by Arch Manning, will likely continue to improve. In terms of explosiveness, however, the Gators have the edge.

Thankfully, the discourse and the comparisons to the conference's elite won't matter much one month from now. In back-to-back weeks, the Gators will play at Texas and against Georgia—games that are likely to feature enormous stakes that impact the conference and beyond.

Just a few short weeks ago, those matchups looked like seismic mismatches on paper. But now? Florida seems every bit up to compete in both.

Sumrall's team, of course, must reach that game of substance unscathed first. Look no further than how Ole Miss struggled to parlay the success from last week into this one.

The hype should be tempered some. That's not just the case for Florida; it's the reality for any team finding enormous success in the month of September.

With that acknowledged, Florida should also be taken seriously. The roster is overflowing with talent, and the offense has the pieces to push any team—no matter how good—to the brink.

If you want to declare Florida "back," go right ahead and don't let anyone tell you otherwise. This team has shown enough in a month of football to let the hope and optimism flow freely.

But why stop there? Think bigger than that. For now, the team has earned it.

articles.title: Alabama Beats South Carolina, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Keelon Russell, Sellers, Top Players
articles.summary: The Alabama Crimson Tide got it done with a dominant 49-18 victory over the LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina Gamecocks at home, fueled by a five-touchdown performance from Keelon Russell.
articles.body:
The Alabama Crimson Tide got it done with a dominant 49-18 victory over the LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina Gamecocks at home, fueled by a five-touchdown performance from Keelon Russell.

Alabama entered Saturday's matchup as a 12.5-point favorite over South Carolina, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

The difference between winning and losing Saturday came through the air. Alabama narrowly edged the Gamecocks in total yards, while South Carolina held the advantage on the ground. The Crimson Tide ultimately separated themselves in the passing game, with Russell throwing for 162 more yards than the Sellers.

5. (24) Mississippi State: 1-0 (CONF), 3-0 (OVR)

10. (14) Tennessee: 0-1 (CONF), 3-1 (OVR)

13. (23) Texas A&M: 0-1 (CONF), 2-1 (OVR)

16. South Carolina: 0-2 (CONF), 2-2 (OVR)

Alabama scored two touchdowns in the first quarter, making a statement early and taking a 14-0 lead. Russell opened the scoring with a 75-yard connection to Lotzeir Brooks for a touchdown before following it up with a 32-yard scoring strike to Ryan Coleman-Williams.

Bama added three more scores in the second quarter, with the most impressive coming from the defense. Defensive back Red Morgan returned an interception 23 yards for a pick-six.

Sellers' highlight of the game came late in the second quarter when he found Nyck Harbor for a deep touchdown connection as the Gamecocks trailed the Crimson Tide 35-10 at the break.

Defense reigned for both teams in the third quarter, with Alabama punting on each of its three possessions and South Carolina punting on both of its drives.

The Gamecocks found the end zone for just the second time in the fourth quarter on a 13-play, 75-yard drive, ending with a Matt Fuller rushing touchdown and a successful two-point conversion to chip away at Alabama's lead.

South Carolina's hopes were quickly squashed as Alabama responded with a Daniel Hill rushing touchdown, a forced fumble and, to put the cherry on top, a touchdown run from Russell to close out the game and secure the 31-point victory.

Alabama will hit the road to face the Mississippi State Bulldogs next Saturday, while South Carolina will look to bounce back at home against the Kentucky Wildcats the same day.

articles.title: Kiffin, LSU Beat TAMU After Ole Miss Loss, Box Score, Top Player Stats, Highlights & SEC Standings
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers bounced back in resounding fashion from their first loss of the season.
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers bounced back in resounding fashion from their first loss of the season.

LSU took down the Texas A&M Aggies, 35-6, in a battle of Top 25 SEC teams.

The win moved the Tigers to 3-1 and got them back on a roll after the road loss to Kiffin's former program, the Ole Miss Rebels, in Week 3.

LSU methodically pulled away from Texas A&M as the game went on.

The Tigers took a 14-3 advantage into halftime thanks to a rushing touchdown from Dilin Jones and a touchdown catch from Jackson Harris.

Harris was one of two LSU wide receivers to eclipse the 100-yard mark on Saturday. He went for 163 yards and two scores on six catches, while Winston Watkins Jr. had five catches for 107 yards.

The Tigers broke the contest open at the start of the second half with a 57-yard touchdown connection between Harris and Sam Leavitt.

Leavitt suffered a leg injury later in the third quarter, which allowed Landen Clark to step in and take more snaps.

Clark ran in a four-yard touchdown to effectively finish off the victory in the middle of the third quarter.

Clark went on to score one more rushing touchdown in the third quarter.

Leavitt's injury will come into focus more once the severity of it is revealed.

LSU can play without Leavitt next week at home against the McNeese Cowboys. The Tigers re-enter SEC play on October 10 versus the Kentucky Wildcats.

articles.title: Dylan Raiola, Jayden Maiava Box Score Stats, Highlights from Oregon vs. USC After Dante Moore Injury
articles.summary: The Oregon Ducks are officially back on track.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks are officially back on track.

Dylan Raiola looked confident under center in place of an injured Dante Moore as the Ducks defeated the USC Trojans 41-27 on the road Saturday.

Heading into Los Angeles, Oregon was a slim 3.5-point favorite over USC and head coach Lincoln Riley, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Moore's injury in the second quarter shifted the energy of the game after the senior quarterback took a hard hit on a targeting call while sliding after picking up a first down.

The targeting call sparked chaos as both teams flooded the field and had to be separated, with Oregon taking offense to USC's Desman Stephens II for the late hit and the celebrations that followed while Moore laid motionless on the field.

Raiola stepped in for Moore and led the Ducks to the win in his first non-blowout minutes at Oregon after spending his freshman and sophomore seasons with the Nebraska Cornhuskers.

5. (7) Ohio State: 1-0 (CONF), 3-1 (OVR)

11. (18) Michigan: 0-1 (CONF), 3-1 (OVR)

12. (13) Penn State: 0-1 (CONF), 3-1 (OVR)

16. Michigan State: 0-1 (CONF), 2-2 (OVR)

In a back-and-forth battle, USC found the end zone first on a 31-yard connection from Maiava to Kayden Dixon-Wyatt.

On the drive Moore began before suffering his injury, Raiola finished it with Oregon's first touchdown of the evening, connecting with Evan Stewart on a short pass before holding up the No. 5 in honor of the starting quarterback.

Both teams added field goals to close out the first half, with Oregon taking a 13-10 lead into the break.

Coming out of halftime, Oregon added two quick touchdowns, totaling just under six minutes of game time, as sophomore running back Dierre Hill Jr. accounted for 12 points for the Ducks.

USC sandwiched a touchdown between Oregon's scores, with Maiava running one in himself before adding a field goal to cut the deficit to 27-20 heading into the final quarter.

Maiava found Tanook Hines for 11 yards to open the fourth-quarter scoring before Oregon went on a fourth-quarter tear.

Raiola found Dakorien Moore for a clutch 29-yard reception just four minutes later. The Ducks defense followed with a big fourth-down stop before the offense converted on a fourth-down opportunity of their own, with Jordon Davison turning it into six points to take a 41-27 lead with just over two minutes remaining.

A lackluster two-minute drill from USC sealed the deal for the Ducks, who walked away with a meaningful road win.

Oregon will take on the other half of Los Angeles, traveling to face the UCLA Bruins after a bye week Oct. 10, while USC will host the Washington Huskies next Saturday.

articles.title: Oregon, USC Scuffle Postgame on Video After Illegal Hit Injured Dante Moore, Knocked QB Out of Game
articles.summary: Oregon and USC got into a postgame scuffle after the Ducks' 41-27 road victory in Los Angeles on Saturday evening.
articles.body:
Oregon and USC got into a postgame scuffle after the Ducks' 41-27 road victory in Los Angeles on Saturday evening.

Tensions were high after USC linebacker Desman Stephens II's late hit in the second quarter on sliding Oregon quarterback Dante Moore led to both teams facing off.

Stephens was flagged and ejected for targeting. Moore was stretchered off the field following the hit and taken to a local hospital. Moore had movement in all of his extremities, per a Ducks' spokesperson .

Dylan Raiola took over at quarterback in Moore's absence.

articles.title: Dan Lanning Rips 'Disgusting' Hit on Dante Moore That Injured QB, Shades USC After Oregon's Win
articles.summary: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning wasn't pleased with the hit by linebacker Desman Stephens II that injured Ducks quarterback Dante Moore during Saturday's matchup between the two teams.
articles.body:
Oregon head coach Dan Lanning wasn't pleased with the hit by linebacker Desman Stephens II that injured Ducks quarterback Dante Moore during Saturday's matchup between the two teams.

"It's a disgusting play," Lanning said after the game, per Sports Illustrated's Bryan Fischer .

As Moore was scrambling for a first down in the second quarter, he started to slide before he was hit by Stephens above the shoulders. Stephens was ejected from the game for targeting.

Moore stayed down on the ground following the collision before he was eventually stretchered off the field and taken to a local hospital for further evaluation. He had feeling in all his extremities, per the NBC broadcast .

Oregon ultimately defeated USC, 41-27, as backup quarterback Dylan Raiola filled in for Moore and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns.

articles.title: Juan Ayuso, colíder de España: “¿Firmar un bronce? Para nada, creo que el oro es posible"
articles.standfirst: El ciclista español habla con MARCA antes del Mundial de Montreal: repasa su estado de forma, el Tour, su futuro y sus ambiciones
articles.summary: El ciclista español habla con MARCA antes del Mundial de Montreal: repasa su estado de forma, el Tour, su futuro y sus ambiciones
articles.body: Juan Ayuso vuelve a sentirse como quiere. Después de un año marcado por caídas, enfermedades y un Tour que define como una decepción, el español llega al Mundial con sensaciones que no encontraba desde febrero. Y con una idea que no necesita rodeos: ganar. Pregunta. España está firmando un Mundial espectacular, con cinco medallas antes incluso de vuestra carrera. Héctor Álvarez ya ha conseguido dos y Benjamín Noval ha sido campeón del mundo júnior. ¿Cómo se vive dentro de la selección lo que están haciendo los jóvenes? ¿Os da más ganas o mete algo de presión de cara al domingo? Respuesta. Presión no. La verdad es que es una alegría porque yo he pasado por categorías inferiores y he compartido tiempo con el staff. Ver las alegrías que están teniendo es una alegría. He seguido muy de cerca a Héctor, que es compañero de equipo mío, y he estado hablando bastante con él. Me da pena que se haya quedado tan cerca del oro dos veces, pero ya ha demostrado qué corredor es. P. Valverde ha hablado de Enric Mas y usted como las dos grandes cartas de España para este Mundial. ¿Llega a Montreal sintiéndose realmente preparado para pelear por una medalla e incluso por el arcoíris? R. Sí, sin duda. Si no, no estaría aquí. La preparación ha sido muy buena, a diferencia de lo que tuve antes del Tour, así que estoy muy contento. Creo que he llegado muy bien y aspiramos a todo. P. Son 274 kilómetros y cerca de 3.800 metros de desnivel, pero sin una subida larguísima que rompa por sí sola la carrera. ¿Qué tipo de Mundial espera? ¿Puede pasar de todo desde muy lejos? R. Creo que puede ser parecido a la carrera que tuvimos hace casi dos semanas, cuando corrimos con equipos. Lo único es que ahora corremos con selecciones y todo cambia. No hay selecciones tan fuertes como sí hay equipos. En la Clásica de Montreal de hace dos semanas era diferente. Veo a Francia intentando endurecer un poco, como hicieron UAE o Decathlon hace dos semanas, y creo que eso nos beneficia. P. El año pasado, cuando atacan Tadej e Isaac del Toro en Ruanda, intenta seguirles y quizá se ceba ahí. ¿Puede ocurrir algo similar? ¿Cómo respondería esta vez? R. Intentaré no atacar a 100 kilómetros. Ya lo probé hace dos semanas y no funcionó. Espero estar a 100 kilómetros un poco más tapado de lo que estuve hace dos semanas o el año pasado. Al final, un Mundial se abre súper pronto y no se corre por equipos, así que es muy difícil controlar. Va a haber situaciones en las que, si hay un grupo por delante, será súper difícil controlar. Hay que estar vivo. Creo que Enric también está bien y, con más bazas, es un poco más fácil jugarlo. P. ¿No le genera incertidumbre cómo han sido las últimas semanas, con esa caída y todo lo que ha pasado? R. Está claro que la caída en Quebec no fue fácil y fue una leche buena, pero me he recuperado bastante bien. Estas dos semanas antes de venir aquí me he encontrado bien. Son los entrenamientos en los que mejor me he encontrado prácticamente en todo el año, con las sensaciones que tenía en febrero antes de Algarve, que no las había vuelto a tener desde entonces. No las tuve antes del Tour. Estoy muy contento con cómo llego y espero que el domingo tenga esas mismas sensaciones. Creo que con eso podemos estar peleando delante. P. No habíamos podido hablar desde el Tour. ¿Qué sensación le dejó? El resultado quizá no fue todo lo positivo que esperaba. ¿Qué análisis ha hecho en frío? R. Por el resultado fue una decepción, evidentemente. Íbamos a por más. El análisis en frío es un poco lo que acabo de comentar: la preparación. Ya antes incluso de llegar al Tour sabía que no estaba, por ejemplo, en mi nivel de Algarve o París-Niza antes de la caída. Tenía la esperanza de que dentro de la carrera fuera mejorando, pero no fue el caso, fue al revés. Son aprendizajes. Creo que el año que viene lo afrontaremos un poco diferente y, evidentemente, ojalá no tenga tantos contratiempos con caídas y enfermedades. El Tour fue una decepción y lo he usado como motivación para preparar bien esta última parte de la temporada. P. Cada año ha ido dando un paso desde aquel podio tan llamativo en su primera gran vuelta. ¿Entiende que haya quien pueda decir que Juan Ayuso se ha estancado? R. En resultados lo podría entender. Al final, si no analizas, mi mejor resultado en una gran vuelta fue la primera que hice. Físicamente, para nada, porque cada año lo llevo mejorando. Además, en este ciclismo, si no mejoras es que empeoras, porque todo el mundo da pasos agigantados año tras año. Hice una muy buena preparación antes de Algarve y París-Niza y fue súper bien. No la pude hacer antes del Tour y ahora sí que la he vuelto a hacer. Creo que estoy muy bien y espero que en el Mundial, Europeo y Lombardía, que son las tres importantes que quedan, le pueda dar la vuelta. P. Hablando de las medallas, ¿firmaría ahora un bronce? R. No. Volvemos a la misma pregunta. Me volverán a decir lo que quieran, pero para nada. Me he probado muy bien, creo que el oro es posible. Luego, si hago plata, bronce, quinto, décimo o vigésimo, habrá que ver cómo va la carrera y seguramente esté orgulloso de haber dado todo, pero salimos a ganar y veremos qué pasa el domingo. P. En Lidl-Trek van a llegar muchos gallos tipo Gall y quizá se vayan algunos como Ciccone. ¿Le preocupa de alguna manera? ¿Cómo analiza las posibles llegadas y salidas? R. Para nada. Mientras el equipo se refuerce y traigamos más corredores de este estilo, por ejemplo Félix Gall, que ha demostrado que es uno de los mejores vueltómanos ahora mismo y ha hecho dos podios este mismo año, son más que bienvenidos. Al final, aporta a toda la estructura y hace que no caiga todo el peso sobre mí, digámoslo así. El equipo se quiere convertir en el mejor equipo del mundo y, si no haces estos fichajes, es imposible conseguirlo. P. ¿Se arrepintió de no ir a LaVuelta? ¿Pensó al verla desde casa que podía haber estado ahí? R. Sin duda. Cuando la veía por la tele... Yo ya le dije al equipo, antes incluso del Tour, que había corrido muy poco al principio del año por todas las caídas y demás, y pregunté si me dejaban esa puerta abierta. Me dijeron que después del Tour lo veríamos. En mi mente estaba hacer LaVuelta, pero terminé tan mal el Tour que no era la decisión sensata, también teniendo en cuenta mi edad. Ya le he dicho al equipo que el año que viene sí que no me dejaré en casa. Este año tuvimos que tomar la decisión más con la cabeza que con el corazón, aunque sí que me costó verla por la tele. P. ¿El año que viene puede ser Giro y LaVuelta o el Tour es innegociable? R. Creo que hacer Tour, Mundial y LaVuelta sería un calendario muy bonito. No he hablado nada con el equipo, así que a lo mejor luego ellos vienen y me dicen que tengo que hacer el Giro. Puede ser. Aún no sé nada, pero me gustaría hacer Tour y LaVuelta. P. Benjamín Noval se marcha de aquí con dos arcoíris. ¿Da algo de envidia ver lo que está consiguiendo? R. Envidia para nada. Es una pasada. Estoy súper contento no solo por él, sino por España en general, porque sigamos sacando talentos así. Me da un poco más de envidia pensar que yo no tuve un Mundial en juveniles de segundo año por el COVID y no lo pude disputar. Esa experiencia de disputar un Mundial estando muy bien en una categoría inferior no la he podido vivir. Pero el éxito de Benja es una pasada y me siento súper orgulloso de que saquemos talentos así. Pronto va a estar en el World Tour y seguro que nos va a seguir dando alegrías. P. Acaba de cumplir 24 años. ¿Qué es lo que más ilusión le hace ahora mismo: ganar una gran vuelta, vestirse algún día de arcoíris o hay alguna otra carrera especialmente marcada? R. Me haces esa pregunta en días de Mundial, así que te tengo que decir un Mundial. Es lo que llevo en mente durante meses. Si me haces la pregunta en diciembre, a lo mejor te digo ganar una gran vuelta antes que el Mundial, pero justo ahora mismo solo está el Mundial en mente.
