articles.title: España se enfrenta a lo (im)posible
articles.standfirst: Disputa la final del Mundial Sub'20 ante una Corea del Norte que es vigentes campeona y suma 13 victorias seguidas en esta categoría
articles.summary: Disputa la final del Mundial Sub'20 ante una Corea del Norte que es vigentes campeona y suma 13 victorias seguidas en esta categoría
articles.body: España buscará este domingo (18:00 horas) la reconquista del Mundial Sub'20 ante una Corea del Norte que defenderá título en el Stadion Miejski de Lodz. Ambas selecciones llegan al último envite invictas, siendo el combinado europeo el más goleador (21) y el asiático el menos goleado (0). Una lucha entre dos modelos exitosos de juego, un pulso entre dos de las canteras más prolíficas del fútbol mundial. "El primer objetivo era llegar a la final, pero no nos vamos a quedar aquí. Queremos ganar", sentencia Daniela Agote, uno de los puntales del equipo dirigido por David Aznar que llega tras ser MVP en semifinales ante Italia. "Somos un equipo con mucha ambición que siempre sale a ganar, dominante, con personalidad, que puede jugar un fútbol combinativo, pero también ser vertical. Sabemos lo que supone jugar una final y queremos ofrecer nuestra mejor versión para llevarnos el título", advierte. Agote es una de las veteranas del equipo con 20 años recién cumplidos. Sabe lo que es ganar el Europeo Sub'19 en dos ocasiones (2024 -donde fue elegida MVP del torneo- y 2025), pero quiere la corona mundial. "Debemos hacer nuestro juego, seguir mostrando esa filosofía que tenemos con balón y dejarnos todo en el campo. Sabemos que enfrente tendremos una selección complicada que ha llegado hasta la final por méritos propios, pero la idea es centrarnos en nosotras mismas", comenta. Será la tercera final de un Mundial Sub'20 para España tras la derrota de 2018 (ante Japón) y la victoria de 2022 (frente a Colombia); y la cuarta de Corea del Norte tras la derrota de 2008 (ante Estados Unidos) y las victorias de 2006 (ante China), 2016 (frente a Francia) y 2024 (ante Japón). "España es un equipo con muchas cualidades. Son especialmente fuertes técnicamente. Nos hemos preparado para enfrentarlos lo mejor posible, con todas nuestras fortalezas", apuntó Han Chol-hak, seleccionador norcoreano. "Tenemos un grado de unión que otras selecciones no tienen. Usaremos esa fortaleza para vencer a España", añadió Pak Ok-I, la capitana de una selección que suma 13 victorias seguidas en esta categoría [récord absoluto]. Intensidad, solidaridad y calidad son las señas de identidad de esta selección dirigida por un Aznar que no sabe lo que es perder un partido desde que llegara a la Federación (ocho victorias y dos empates con la Sub'19 y nueve victorias con la Sub'20). "Es un entrenador que nos da mucha confianza. Yo tuve la suerte de coincidir con él en el Athletic Club y cuando me enteré que venía a las categorías inferiores me alegré porque creo que sabe sacar lo mejor de nosotras", revela Agote, la '11' del equipo. "Es un número que me gusta desde siempre, sin más. ¿De jugona? Puede ser", dice entre risas. La finalísima se jugará en el Stadion Miejski, un coliseo con capacidad para 18.029 espectadores donde la afición española -escasa, pero ruidosa- quiere hacerse notar otra vez. "Es un plus para nosotras tener a nuestros familiares en las gradas. Ojalá podamos celebrar con ellos el título", sentencia Agote. "Llevamos soñando con este día desde que empezamos la concentración. Hemos llegado hasta aquí disfrutando mucho y queremos hacerlo hasta el último minuto", subraya.

articles.title: España siembra el pánico
articles.standfirst: La campeona del mundo lanza en Wembley un mensaje de ser indomable
articles.summary: La campeona del mundo lanza en Wembley un mensaje de ser indomable
articles.body: La selección española estrenó la segunda estrella con una victoria de las que dejan huella. Lo hizo en un escenario único como Wembley y de una manera que refuerza su condición de campeona del mundo. España dominó durante muchos minutos, acumuló ocasiones claras de gol y demostró personalidad cuando el partido se complicó. Tras adelantarse en el marcador, supo resistir la poderosa reacción inglesa y acabar imponiéndose para firmar un triunfo de prestigio por 1-2 en el templo del fútbol. La tercera conquista de Wembley en diez visitas (1981, 2018 y 2026) fue la más brillante. La más impactante. Porque España dejó la impronta de un equipo dominante, capaz de salir en busca de la victoria en cualquier escenario. Porque el poderoso frente ofensivo llevó a los de Luis de la Fuente a un escenario en el que muchos equipos se habrían derrumbado ante la avalancha del final de la primera parte y la puesta en escena de la segunda. El asombro por cómo se movió España en Wembley estaba en las palabras de todos los comentaristas de las televisiones británicas. "Miras a España y notas una cosa: el momento de los pases. Ese es un equipo que tiene una identidad. Conocen sus fortalezas, saben adónde va el próximo pase y todos se ven cómodos en el sistema. Nosotros tnemos jugadores increíbles, pero tener buenos jugadores no te convierte automáticamente en un buen equipo. En este momento, Inglaterra parece una colección de individuos en lugar de un equipo. España lo es", explicaba James Carragher. Las palabras de elogio recorrían la prensa mundial tras el partido de Wembley. "España estira su invicto", se leía en Olé. El diario argentino destacaba la forma en la que la selección española amplió hasta 40 su racha de partidos oficiales sin perder. Un registro que hace tiempo se convirtió en el mejor de su historia y que no deja de crecer. Esa mano de hierro con la que España domina el mundo en su segunda edad de oro presenta una fisonomía que justifica el temor que ha desatado entre sus rivales. En el camino recorrido desde la derrota del 28 de marzo de 2023 en Glasgow, la selección ha derrotado a seis de las otras siete campeonas del mundo: Argentina, Uruguay, Alemania, Francia (tres veces), Inglaterra (dos) e Italia (dos). Con Brasil no se ha medido en partidos oficiales. Entre las campeonas de Europa, ha vencido a franceses, alemanes, italianos, portugueses, daneses y checos. Con Rusia no ha jugado y a Holanda la eliminó en los cuartos de la pasada Nations League tras empatar los dos partidos y resolver la eliminatoria en los penaltis de Mestalla. La sensación de poder de España se amplía si se analiza el cómo. De la Fuente ha generado un ecosistema dominante desde escenarios muy distintos. La selección ha mantenido su línea ganadora a pesar de la acumulación de bajas que para otro equipo sería un virus demoledor: Unai, Carvajal, Laporte, Rodri, Lamine Yamal, Nico, Morata... En diferentes momentos han entrado jugadores que han mantenido e incluso elevado el nivel de juego del equipo que causó admiración en la Eurocopa: Raya, Cubarsí, Pedro Porro, Zubimendi, Baena, Oyarzabal... El partido ante Inglaterra fue un ejemplo de madurez. España se puso en marcha con una primera media en la que pudo lograr una diferencia escandalosa. Pero al descanso se fue perdiendo y a punto estuvo de verse con 3-1 en el marcador. Entonces apareció el equipo capaz de cambiar de registro, de marcha. De la Fuente mandó al campo a Pedri, Oyarzabal y Baena y el partido viró hacia un lugar en el que España desactivo la reacción inglesa y el equipo de Tuchel fue incapaz de entender qué pasaba, por qué lo que era viento a favor paso a ser una tempestad que la llevó a zozobrar. Llegará la derrota, porque es ley del fútbol. Pero España ha logrado que cada rival que tiene delante, por muy superpotencia que sea, como es el caso de Inglaterra, piense que se enfrenta a un coloso. A un enemigo al que sólo podrá vencer si baja la guardia. Y esta España, como se vio en Wembley, no está por la labor de dar facilidades ni de levantar la bandera blanca cuando la situación se pone peliaguda.

articles.title: Di María gana la Supercopa con polémica y gran enfado de la 'Brujita' Verón: "Es toda tuya, ladrón"
articles.standfirst: Rosario Central gana con doblete del 'Fideo' remontando el gol inicial de Alexis Castro, en un encuentro marcado por la tensión, polémicas arbitrales y una fuerte tángana al final
articles.summary: Rosario Central gana con doblete del 'Fideo' remontando el gol inicial de Alexis Castro, en un encuentro marcado por la tensión, polémicas arbitrales y una fuerte tángana al final
articles.body: Rosario Central conquistó Supercopa Internacional tras derrotar por 3-1 a Estudiantes de La Plata en el estadio Madre de Ciudades de Santiago del Estero, sumando así el decimocuarto título de su historia (cinco campeonatos de Primera División y nueve copas nacionales). Un título que quedará marcado por la gran polémica arbitral durante el partido y con Di María como gran protagonista por marcar un doblete. El encuentro enfrentó al líder de la tabla anual de 2025 con el vencedor del Trofeo de Campeones de ese mismo año. Sin embargo, el título quedó empañado por un escandaloso final que incluyó agresiones entre futbolistas y las acusaciones de la 'Brujita' Verón al árbitro Darío Herrera, que ni siquiera pudo señalar el pitido final. El partido comenzó con máxima intensidad desde el primer segundo. A los 53 segundos, Alexis Castro adelantó a Estudiantes tras empujar un centro de Guido Carrillo. Pese al gol tempranero y a las lesiones de dos futbolistas del conjunto platense —incluyendo la evacuación en ambulancia del uruguayo Gabriel Neves por una lesión en la muñeca—, Rosario Central logró la igualada gracias a un muy inspirado Ángel Di María, que empató con un gran gol de falta imitando a su amigo Messi. La remontada rosarina se culminó antes del descanso con un gol de penalti transformado por Di María, que firmaba así el doblete. Ahí surgió una de las grandes polémicas del encuentro. La pena máxima, cobrada a instancias del VAR tras un contacto entre Leandro González Pirez y Enzo Copetti, enfureció al cuatro platense. Tanto, que el propio Verón no dudó en comentar al respecto: “La impunidad que manejan para robarte es increíble. Innecesario. ¿Para esto nos traen hasta acá? Jajaja, una puesta en escena ridícula”. Así llegaron hasta el añadido de la segunda parte. Fernando Muslera, portero de Estudiantes, subió para intentar rematar a la desesperada, pero no tuvieron éxito y a la contra Julián Fernández anotó el 1-3 definitivo. Y ahí empezó la guerra. Un grave enfrentamiento con empujones y puñetazos entre jugadores de ambos equipos que obligó a una retirada apresurada hacia vestuarios antes de poder reanudar el juego. En medio del tumulto, el presidente de Estudiantes, la 'Brujita' Verón, bajó al campo para dirigirse al árbitro con la frase: "Es toda tuya, ladrón", reavivando una enemistad institucional surgida en noviembre de 2025 tras la controversia por el reconocimiento de la AFA a Central.

articles.title: Tony Pulis column: 'I feel cheated - when do Stoke City get our FA Cup?'
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains what he and all Stoke fans are thinking after Manchester City are found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges they faced.
articles.body:
That is what all Stoke City fans have been asking me since the news broke on Friday that Manchester City had been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they have been accused of breaching.

While the process is far from over because Manchester City are expected to appeal, I have to say this verdict and the whole situation has left a very sour taste in my mouth.

Taking my Stoke side to the 2011 FA Cup final was one of the highlights - if not THE highlight - of my 50 years in football as a player and manager.

That day in May will also live long in the memory of all Stoke fans who followed their team to Wembley dreaming that they would win the greatest club cup competition in world football for the first time in their long history.

The club we were playing, Manchester City , were on their way to dominating English football.

At that time they had not won a major trophy for 35 years but they were a team that, in transfer fees and wages, cost well above anything Stoke City could ever aspire to.

Think back now, and I can still picture walking out before kick-off to see our end of the ground decked in red and white and hear the amazing rendition of Delilah from our supporters.

Many of those fans had come from all corners of the world, and had spent or borrowed fortunes to make it, just to say: "I was there."

For me, experiencing that game and occasion with Stoke City's owners, the Coates family, was really touching too.

Continuously, over many decades, they have helped to finance their own community's local professional team.

For Peter, Denise, John and all the family and friends who in good times and bad found the money and spirit to back the club, it was their one day in the sun.

It was the same for all of us connected with Stoke. This was our day, that day that many smaller clubs and their fans pray for.

Although we lost 1-0, our players were fantastic and gave, as always, a fully committed performance against the odds.

Yaya Toure, who scored the winning goal, was reportedly earning 10 times what we were paying any of our players and, on his own, had cost more than our entire starting 11 when they had signed him from Barcelona in 2010.

After the game, my disappointment was buried in the fact we had played a team full of superstars, and faced an elite coach in Roberto Mancini, and had just fallen short.

Today, I feel very differently, as I am sure people connected with the other clubs affected by City's successes in the same period, between 2009 and 2018, do too.

We lost, but to a team that have been found guilty of breaking the financial rules set out by the Premier League.

In doing so, they did not just beat Stoke in an FA Cup final, they collected a stack of titles and went on to completely dominate English football for more than a decade.

So, with those rules having been broken, what will the punishment be?

Well, I know all Stoke supporters will be demanding that City pass the trophy over and every club that has been affected by their actions will be considering their legal options.

I don't expect Manchester City to phone me or the club up and offer back the 2011 FA Cup and the winners' medals their players received.

I don't seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either. A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely.

But I still feel cheated. Whatever happens next, we won't ever get that day back and the chance to celebrate around Stoke-on-Trent with the cup and medals we so honestly fought for. After breaking the rules, Manchester City got to do that instead.

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

articles.title: Norway vs Portugal: UEFA Nations League – Ronaldo, Haaland, teams, form
articles.summary: Norway host two-time UEFA Nations League winners Portugal in Oslo in the second match of the league phase.
articles.body:
Who : Norway vs Portugal What : UEFA Nations League 2026-2027 , Group A4 match Where : Ullevaal Stadion in Oslo, Norway When : Sunday at 7:45pm (18:45 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 15:45 GMT.

Record two-time UEFA Nations League champions Portugal continue their title defence on matchday two with a trip to Oslo against an exciting Norway side.

After starting their campaign with a 1-0 home win over Wales , holders Portugal face their first big test of the competition on Sunday against the Norwegians, who defied expectations with a historic quarterfinal finish at this year’s FIFA World Cup .

Spearheaded by Erling Haaland, arguably one of Europe’s most dangerous strikers, and captained by midfield maestro Martin Odegaard, Norway made a winning start too, beating their Scandinavian rivals Denmark 3-2 in a thrilling opener.

Frustrated after a string of missed chances in the first game, Portugal’s talisman Cristiano Ronaldo will hope to rediscover his form as the team embraces a new chapter under coach Jorge Jesus, whose first game in charge was on Thursday against Wales.

The UEFA Nations League was founded in 2018 to reduce the number of meaningless friendlies and give nations competitive matches against equally ranked teams.

In this competition, countries from across Europe participate in a league structure that features promotion and relegation.

The teams last met in a 2016 international friendly in Porto when hosts Portugal defeated Norway 3-0.

Haaland and Oscar Bobb (Norway): A double from Haaland and another goal from Bobb set Norway on course for a winning start, and the attacking pair should be in the limelight in front of their home crowd this weekend. Manchester City’s Haaland, especially, has been in top form this term with an incredible seven goals in as many games across all competitions.

Ronaldo and Joao Felix (Portugal): Portugal’s striking pair of Ronaldo and Felix ought to be careful in the final third this time out after Felix’s lone strike in the opening win in Lisbon. Ronaldo had a goal ruled out and was among the players who missed a flurry of chances as Portugal registered a whopping 23 total shots but with only five on target, of which just one hit the back of the net.

Will Haaland, Ronaldo and Bruno Fernandes play?

Both forwards are fit to play, but Portugal will miss the services of their talismanic midfielder Bruno Fernandes, who is injured.

Fernandes has played in all seven of Manchester United’s matches this season and featured from the start for Portugal against Wales before being withdrawn in the 90th minute.

Jesus said he doesn’t want to “risk” the player against Norway.

“Against Wales, we went in with practically everyone physically available and came out with a complicated problem with Bruno Fernandes,” the coach said.

“He’s coming off an injury at United, and he told me he’s been playing with that pain for the last three games, which is hindering him.

“It was one of the factors that prevented Bruno from playing at his best against Wales. I’ve already spoken to him, and I prefer not to risk it in this game, so he’s fully fit for the Denmark match.”

Haaland’s double against Denmark on Thursday marked another milestone in the 26-year-old striker’s enviable career. He is now the highest-scoring Nordic man in international football history, surpassing Sweden’s Zlatan Ibrahimovic.

Haaland’s goal tally for Norway stands at 64 goals compared with Ibrahimovic’s 62. Incredibly, Haaland has shattered that record in 56 appearances – less than half of the 122 matches Ibrahimovic needed.

“It is not possible to explain nor ‌‌is it possible to learn. He is born with it. It is instinct,” Norway manager Stale Solbakken said about Haaland.

Having made his senior debut in 2019, Haaland boasts a record of scoring more than one goal per game for Norway.

“It’s madness,” midfielder Sander Berge said about Haaland’s talent. “It’s everyday business that Haaland scores goals, so it’s reasonable that he is up there, but it’s ⁠⁠powerful.”

Jesus: “Norway are one of the strongest teams in Europe. They have players we know like Haaland and Odegaard who play at a very high level in England. They will create more goalscoring opportunities against us than Wales, and I hope we have the defensive capacity.

“There’s not much to improve. We’ll evolve the game we’ve already played, but I trust that the team will respond defensively and will be more creative offensively.”

Solbakken: “They changed the coach, and if you look at what he did at his previous clubs and the football they played, the way they played against Wales was a little different to what it was with [Roberto] Martinez. There were players in other positions, and we took that into account in our game plan. Obviously, they have good players all over the field. We expect a close and balanced game. It’s our home game, so we’ll try to stop their biggest assets, but it’s also important for us to play our game and be loyal to the way we’ve been playing in recent years.”

Have Haaland and Ronaldo ever played each other?

No, the 26-year-old and 41-year-old greats have never crossed paths. Norway and Portugal have not played each other frequently either.

Norway will be without David Moller Wolfe, who is suspended after picking up two yellow cards in the last game.

articles.title: England push Spain to the limit in 3-2 thriller as Anthony Gordon claims “no gap” between the sides
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon is confident England can compete with the very best after a narrow Nations League loss to world champions Spain.Spain secured a 3-2 win at Wem...
articles.body:
Anthony Gordon is confident England can compete with the very best after a narrow Nations League loss to world champions Spain .

Spain secured a 3-2 win at Wembley in the Nations League opener, in a chaotic clash that saw the lead change hands on three occasions.

The world champions led inside two minutes when Lamine Yamal capitalised on an error from Marc Guehi to open the scoring, but England fought back to lead at half-time. Gordon got the leveller after finishing off a lightning counter from the Three Lions, before Harry Kane headed home from Nico O'Reilly's cross, via a deflection.

Kane spurned the chance to extend England's lead when his penalty crashed off the woodwork, and Spain punished the hosts as goals from Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal turned the game around.

Gordon insists England can match world champions after wild 3-2 Nations League loss to Spain at Wembley

Spain extended their unbeaten run to 39 games in normal time and Gordon said England can take heart from pushing the World Cup winners all the way.

The Barcelona winger said he does not see 'a gap' between Thomas Tuchel's side and Spain.

"I don't think there is a gap [to Spain] I feel like we're right there," Gordon told ITV Sport.

"We can win that game so easily. If the penalty goes in we can go on and win the game. In hindsight it's always easy to say that. But I felt good in the game.

"I don't think there is a gap and I think if we played them in the final I would've felt confident. Being confident doesn't always translate into a win, but I think you've seen here tonight that we're a top team."

articles.title: Kylian Mbappe’s knee injury to keep him out for two weeks
articles.summary: Mbappe suffers hyperextension of left knee against Turkiye but is expected to be fit to face Barcelona in El Clasico.
articles.body:
France captain Kylian Mbappe has suffered a hyperextension of his left knee while playing for France, his club Real Madrid says, but the forward could be ready to play again when La Liga resumes.

“Following tests carried out today by Real Madrid’s medical department on our player Kylian Mbappe, he has been diagnosed with a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee,” the Spanish club said in a statement on Saturday.

The forward left the pitch shortly after opening the scoring in a 1-0 French win against Turkiye on Friday. He winced in pain as his teammates came across to celebrate the goal, his 67th for France, at Kocaeli Stadium in Izmit, about 100km (60 miles) southeast of Istanbul.

Mbappe tried to carry on after receiving treatment but eventually slumped to the ground and looked concerned as he prodded the outside of his left knee before walking off to be replaced by Desire Doue.

New coach Zinedine Zidane said France were “not going to take any risks” and he would not use Mbappe in the three Nations League matches scheduled over the next 10 days.

France travel to Belgium on Monday before hosting Italy and Belgium at the Stade de France on October 2 and 5.

Real Madrid’s first game after the international break against Villarreal on October 10 might be too soon for a Mbappe return, but Spanish daily AS reported on Saturday that he would certainly be ready for the Clasico with Barcelona on October 25.

articles.title: Real Madrid learn extent of Kylian Mbappe injury after France scare
articles.summary: Despite the several new additions they made to their squad during the last summer transfer window, the start of the 2026-27 season has been far from ideal fo...
articles.body:
Despite the several new additions they made to their squad during the last summer transfer window, the start of the 2026-27 season has been far from ideal for Real Madrid . The Merengues have already lost two games in La Liga, to Real Betis and Atletico Madrid , putting them six points behind an FC Barcelona team that seems unstoppable whenever it takes to the pitch.

Meanwhile, physical problems have also started piling up for Los Blancos lately. Ferland Mendy , Eder Militao , and Rodrygo Goes were already unavailable at the start of the season because of their injuries from the last season, while Federico Valverde also suffered an injury during the game against Atletico.

Things got only worse during the September international break. First, it was Ibrahima Konate who suffered an injury while training with France, and he returned to Real Madrid to recover without playing a single minute for his new national team coach, Zinedine Zidane.

Then, Kylian Mbappe set off alarms bells at Valdebebas as he showed serious signs of pain right after scoring for France in the game against Turkiye. The Frenchman was substituted off a few minutes later, and Zidane made it clear that the forward would have to return to the Spanish capital because of the injury .

As Diario AS has reported, detailed tests have now been conducted, and their results have brought significant relief for Real Madrid. These results show Mbappe is suffering from a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of the left knee, which will keep him out of action for 10-12 days.

Thus, Kylian Mbappe will not only be available for the upcoming El Clasico on October 25, but also for the difficult run of games leading up to it, which will see them face opponents like Villarreal , Roma, Sevilla, and RB Leipzig . However, it still needs to be seen how he will progress in his recovery during the next few weeks.

articles.title: Former Liverpool boss’ previous comments could cost him after City ruling
articles.summary: Jurgen Klopp, Man City Charges and the Promise That Still Hangs Over Liverpool’s Near-Miss TitlesThere are stories in football that sit quietly in the backgr...
articles.body:
Jurgen Klopp, Man City Charges and the Promise That Still Hangs Over Liverpool 's Near-Miss Titles

There are stories in football that sit quietly in the background for years, then suddenly begin to throb with fresh significance. The latest developments around the original source report on Manchester City's charges have done exactly that, pulling Jürgen Klopp's old remarks back into view and reminding Liverpool supporters of two title races that still sting.

City have been found guilty of 114 out of 115 Premier League charges relating to alleged financial irregularities. City have long denied wrongdoing and are expected to appeal, so there is still distance to travel before the game knows the final shape of any punishment. Yet even the possibility of retrospective action revives old wounds on Merseyside.

Man City charges revive old Liverpool pain

Klopp's Liverpool were one of the great modern sides, a team of ferocious quality and conviction. To collect more than 90 points in both 2018/19 and 2021/22 and still finish second left a mark. Those campaigns were never defined by failure, but by the brutal excellence of the opponent standing in the way.

That is why Klopp's comments from January 2025 from the Liverpool Echo have endured. Asked what might happen if Liverpool were eventually handed titles, he said: "Did you say few months or three? Ah okay. We're getting closer." He added: "Should? I don't say anything. Would? We had this discussion when we left, if it would happen I told all the people who want it, just book the flight and I buy the beer."

Klopp Mallorca parade promise still lingers

There was humour in it, naturally, because Klopp always understood how to lighten a moment loaded with grievance. Yet there was something else too, a sense that football's moral ledger does matter. When he continued, "Whatever we have to celebrate, good weather, we would have our own parade in my garden. God what a headline," it sounded playful, but also like a man acknowledging how deeply those narrow misses were felt.

Klopp has since left Red Bull and taken charge of Germany, while Liverpool have moved into a new era under Andoni Iraola . Still, his words remain attached to this case because they captured what many supporters feel. Titles are won on the pitch, in the lungs, in the legs, in the tiny moments that define spring. If any are ever reassigned, the celebration may feel unusual, but the grievance behind it will be real enough.

Premier League fallout could reshape legacy

Liverpool's next league meeting with City on 11 October will carry its own intrigue, as every match between these clubs tends to do. But this issue reaches beyond one fixture. It reaches into legacy, credibility and whether the Premier League can persuade the world that sporting competition has been protected with sufficient force.

If Klopp does end up buying that beer in Mallorca, it will cost him a fair bit. For Liverpool supporters, the emotional bill has already been far higher.

Right then, Mallorca. We are all going, apparently. One minute it is a quiet autumn, the next we are pricing flights, checking passport dates and wondering whether Klopp's garden has room for six thousand Reds, three inflatables and one lad who swears he knows the best kebab place on the island.

This is the part where Liverpool fans try to stay calm and dignified, which lasts about seven seconds. Because if those near-miss titles ever land at Anfield after all this time, nobody is pretending it will be normal. It will be wonderfully weird. There will be songs, there will be flags, and there will definitely be at least one fella claiming he always believed the parade route through a private garden in Mallorca was realistic.

And imagine Klopp on beer duty. Risky promise, that. Liverpool supporters treat free ale like a pressing trigger. One whisper of "I'll buy the beer" and half the fanbase is already in flip-flops at the departure gate.

Still, beneath the jokes is the serious bit. Fans invest years, money, emotion and sanity into title races. So if football tells them those races were bent out of true, of course it matters. Deeply. Even if the celebration arrives late, sunburnt and slightly confused.

For now, we wait. But if this ends with retrospective titles, someone start stretching. We have got a garden parade to win.

articles.title: Los azulgranas, protagonistas en la primera jornada de selecciones
articles.standfirst: Únicamente Eric García, con molestias, y Fermín no tuvieron minutos
articles.summary: Únicamente Eric García, con molestias, y Fermín no tuvieron minutos
articles.body: La primera jornada del parón de selecciones puso el sábado por la noche su punto y final y, en clave azulgrana, los jugadores del Barcelona han sido protagonistas en todos los partidos. Únicamente Eric García, que iba a ser titular pero notó unas molestias en la rodilla, y Fermín se han quedado sin disputar ningún minuto. El resto de culés, con sus respectivas selecciones, han tenido presencia. Los primeros en jugar, ya el pasado jueves, fueron Cancelo, con Portugal; Adeyemi, con Alemania; y Bisiwu, con la sub-21 de Bélgica. El luso es un futbolista clave en su combinado y fue sustituido en el 90' contra Gales. El atacante alemán, por su parte, jugó 80 minutos y dio una asistencia. En el caso del joven extremo, firmado este verano por el Barcelona, solo tuvo cinco minutos, pero supusieron su estreno con su selección. El viernes entraron en escena Raphinha, Koundé, Bernal, Xavi Espart y Hamza. En el caso del brasileño, que actuó como mediapunta, completó todo el encuentro contra Australia. El lateral francés también estuvo todo el partido sobre el césped en el triunfo de su combinado contra Turquía. Xavi Espart y Marc Bernal fueron titulares en la derrota de la sub-21, pero el zaguero solo disputó una parte, mientras que el mediocentro completó todo el choque. En el caso de Hamza, saltó al verde a falta de media hora para el final. Ayer sábado fue el turno de Livakovic y de la nutrida representación azulgrana en el Inglaterra-España. Tras debutar el meta con la camiseta del Barcelona en el último encuentro de LaLiga contra el Sevilla, el croata fue titular con su selección y sumó un triunfo antes de medirse el martes, precisamente, a España. El partido en Wembley contaba con ocho azulgranas en total, de los cuales seis estuvieron sobre el verde. Gordon, con el combinado inglés, jugó 70 minutos y marcó una diana. De hecho, el extremo culé fue uno de los destacados de su selección. Por parte de la Roja, Lamine, Rodri y Cubarsí jugaron todo el partido e, incluso, el de Rocafonda anotó un tempranero tanto. Olmo, que también salió de inicio, disputó 82 minutos y Pedri saltó al campo a falta de 20'. Eric, que debía ser titular pero notó molestias en el calentamiento, y Fermín, los únicos inéditos.

articles.body: Las grandes potencias europeas vuelven a la acción este domingo 27 de septiembre en la segunda jornada de la UEFA Nations League. Las principales selecciones del continente saltan al terreno de juego con la obligación de sumar de tres en tres para asegurar su billete hacia la 'Final Four' o, en su defecto, amarrar la permanencia o conseguir el ascenso en la élite tras un inicio de competición exigente. El gran plato fuerte de la fecha lo protagoniza el choque de trenes en el Grupo A, donde los gigantes del fútbol europeo miden sus fuerzas en un duelo de máxima tensión táctica. El partido más destacado será el Noruega - Portugal, emparejados en el Grupo A4. El duelo se disputará en el Ullevaal Stadium de Oslo y enfrentará Haaland contra Cristiano Ronaldo. En la primera jornada, ambos combinados lograron ganar. Los nórdicos vencieron 3-2 a Dinamarca, con un doblete del delantero del City. Portugal arrancó la 'era Jorge Jesús' con un triunfo por la mínima frente a Gales, con un solitario gol de Joao Félix. El otro duelo interesante será el Alemania - Grecia, del grupo A2. Los alemanes se estrenaron de la mano de Klopp con un empate ante Países Bajos. Los helenos, ganaron 2-1 a Serbia y son líderes en la tabla. En el mismo grupo, jugarán Serbia y Países Bajos.

articles.summary: Former Rangers winger Rabbi Matondo is on trial with Hibernian while Torino midfielder Gvidas Gineitis admits joining Celtic would be of interest.
articles.body:
Former Rangers winger Rabbi Matondo is on trial with Hibernian while Torino midfielder Gvidas Gineitis admits joining Celtic would be of interest.

Former Rangers winger Rabbi Matondo has joined Hibernian at their training camp in La Manga as the 26-year-old Wales international looks to win a contract after his summer release by Brann . ( Daily Record , external )

Lithuania midfielder Gvidas Gineitis, the 22-year-old who Celtic pursued this summer, says joining the Scottish champions from Torino "would be an interesting and rewarding experience". ( 15min.It , external )

Sabah Kerjota, the 25-year-old winger who joined Heart of Midlothian from Sambenedettese last year, says his journey from Italy's Serie D to a first call-up by Albania is proof that data-driven recruitment can make dreams come true. ( Daily Record , external )

Rangers goalkeeper Rydnn McGuire turned down offers from English clubs before signing a three-year contract as the 17-year-old sees a pathway to the first team at Ibrox. ( Rangers Review , external )

Bobby Williamson admits his application to be the new Scotland head coach was not realistic despite Ally McCoist, Scott Brown and Kevin Thomson agreeing to be assistants, especially as his European coaching licence lapsed 10 years ago, but suggests his record of leading Kilmarnock to a Scottish Cup win and four regional titles with Uganda is "not a bad career". ( The Scotsman , external )

Former Hamilton Academical owner Gerry Strain plans to take the Scottish Professional Football League to court unless it settles out of court after he challenged the Scottish FA's decision to deem him "not fit and proper" to run the club last year. ( Scottish Sun , external )
